poems.title: There's a certain slant of light
poems.author: emily-dickinson
poems.start: There’s a certain slant of light,
poems.end: On the look of death.

poems.title: A Clear Midnight
poems.author: walt-whitman
poems.start: This is thy hour O Soul, thy free flight into the wordless,
poems.end: Night, sleep, death and the stars.

poems.title: A Noiseless Patient Spider
poems.author: walt-whitman
poems.start: A noiseless patient spider,
poems.end: Till the gossamer thread you fling catch somewhere, O my soul.

poems.title: Spring and Fall
poems.author: gerard-manley-hopkins
poems.start: MÁRGARÉT, áre you gríeving
poems.end: It is Margaret you mourn for.

poems.title: Pied Beauty
poems.author: gerard-manley-hopkins
poems.start: GLORY be to God for dappled things —
poems.end: Praise him.

poems.title: Because I could not stop for Death
poems.author: emily-dickinson
poems.start: Because I could not stop for Death,
poems.end: Were toward eternity.

poems.title: I'm nobody! Who are you?
poems.author: emily-dickinson
poems.start: I’m nobody! Who are you?
poems.end: To an admiring bog!

poems.title: The Pasture
poems.author: robert-frost
poems.start: I’m going out to clean the pasture spring;
poems.end: I sha’n’t be gone long.—You come too.

poems.title: God's Grandeur
poems.author: gerard-manley-hopkins
poems.start: The world is charged with the grandeur of God,
poems.end: World broods with warm breast, and with, ah, bright wings!

poems.title: The Last Invocation
poems.author: walt-whitman
poems.start: At the last, tenderly,
poems.end: Strong is your hold O love.)

poems.title: The Road Not Taken
poems.author: robert-frost
poems.start: Two roads diverged in a yellow wood,
poems.end: And that has made all the difference.

poems.title: Wild nights! Wild nights!
poems.author: emily-dickinson
poems.start: Wild nights! Wild nights!
poems.end: To-night in thee!

poems.title: O Captain! My Captain!
poems.author: walt-whitman
poems.start: O Captain! my Captain! our fearful trip is done,
poems.end: Fallen cold and dead.

poems.title: Heaven-Haven (A Nun Takes the Veil)
poems.author: gerard-manley-hopkins
poems.start: I have desired to go
poems.end: And out of the swing of the sea.

poems.title: October
poems.author: robert-frost
poems.start: O hushed October morning mild,
poems.end: Enchant the land with amethyst.

poems.title: The Birdlet
poems.author: alexander-pushkin
poems.start: IN exile I sacredly observe
poems.end: I could of freedom make a gift?

poems.title: The Cloud
poems.author: alexander-pushkin
poems.start: O last cloud of the scattered storm,
poems.end: Forth chases thee from the quieted heavens.

poems.title: The Trees
poems.author: philip-larkin
poems.source: High Windows (1974); collected in Collected Poems (Faber)
poems.start: The trees are coming into leaf
poems.end: Their greenness is a kind of grief.

poems.title: This is Love
poems.author: rumi
poems.start: This is Love : to fly heavenward,
poems.end: Not to see what appears to one's self.

poems.title: Success is counted sweetest
poems.author: emily-dickinson
poems.start: Success is counted sweetest
poems.end: Break, agonized and clear!

poems.title: Miracles
poems.author: walt-whitman
poems.start: Why, who makes much of a miracle?
poems.end: What stranger miracles are there?

poems.title: Inversnaid
poems.author: gerard-manley-hopkins
poems.start: THIS darksome burn, horseback brown,
poems.end: Long live the weeds and the wilderness yet.

poems.title: Mowing
poems.author: robert-frost
poems.start: There was never a sound beside the wood but one,
poems.end: My long scythe whispered and left the hay to make.
